# The null position is fixed, and underneath it is the defect that caused all of this

RED is record 48 and GREEN is record 49, 1,303 tests, up 26. The RED reproduced record 47's refusal verbatim,
and the mirror failed as it had to, on a refusal that named no file: "'harness/slice_two.py' not found in 'The
tree moved under check 3 ... compared over the whole tree because this citation names no slice'".

A null position now takes the union of every file the accepted plan's slices name, read position by position
through the same function a numbered citation uses, then widened by what the round's own commit moved. Nothing
the citing record says can widen or narrow it: the plan comes from the accepted solution record and the rest
from git, so there is no claim to corroborate. Wider than one slice, narrower than the tree, and wider is
stricter. When another record declares a number for the same check, neither wins and it falls to the whole
tree, because null is a claim rather than a shrug and a claim the chain contradicts settles nothing.

**A premise of record 47 was wrong and is corrected here.** That note said `handoff` and `guard` already take a
union reading. They do not: `guard.decide` allows everything once `handoff.current_slice` returns no entry, with
rule `no-slice-plan`, and there is no `outside-plan` rule in this tree. The real precedent is
`triage.solution_paths` with its slice-files check, which holds every changed file to the union of the plan's
slice files, and that is what the fix follows. The earlier note's reasoning was right and its citation was not.

**And the measurement underneath it, which is the root cause of this whole chain.** SEEN-113's own attempt 5
still cannot cite records 34 and 35, and no longer because of the null position: the scope is granted, the plan
names four files, and the refusal has moved to "no commit on this branch carries the tree it ran against, so
which files moved cannot be told". Measured in a clean worktree: neither green 35's tree nor red 34's is the
content of any of the branch's last sixty commits. Attempt 4's work was committed at `cd9e549`, whose content is
the tree the review check ran against, **because the ticket file was rewritten between the green and the commit**
with the status, the ticks and the Outcome. The counterfactual was measured too: had the green's tree been the
committed one, the citation would still be refused, on the ticket file alone.

So the thing that blocks a citation is the harness's own required step. The procedure says write the `## Outcome`,
set `status: review` and tick the criteria **before** leaving review, so the ticket file is guaranteed to change
between a check and the commit that carries its work, and the fingerprint counts the ticket file. Both
`FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDED` and `triage`'s slice-files check already exempt exactly that class of path, for exactly
this reason, and the commit search does not.

That is the next defect and it is not fixed here, because the fix is a design decision rather than a correction.
The fingerprint must keep covering the whole ticket file, which is what gives the receipt its meaning and is what
SEEN-109 withdrew an attempt to weaken; so what has to become tolerant is the search for the commit carrying a
check's tree, not the fingerprint itself. Naming it is worth more than a fourth consecutive round on this ticket
begun without a decision.

SEEN-112 was re-measured on its branch for the fourth time and nothing widened: all five pairs refused, greens 11
and 15 by name on the reworked files, and the null round's green 24 refused because the plan names a test file
the attempt-5 replan added which git cannot see in the tree that check ran against.
